newsitem.title: USA: Henkel launches $1.12 billion bid for Loctite.
newsitem.headline: Henkel launches $1.12 billion bid for Loctite.

text.p: German consumer products maker Henkel KGaA said Monday it plans to gain control of chemical maker Loctite Corp. for 1.7 billion German marks ($1.12 billion).

Duesseldorf, Germany-based Henkel currently owns 35 percent of Loctite, a maker of speciality chemicals used for adhesives and sealants. It said it is offering to buy the remaining 65 percent stake for $56 per share.
Loctite's stock was up sharply on the news, jumping $11.875 to $57.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Loctite said it would review the proposal from its largest shareholder.

"The company, its board of directors and management, and their various advisers, will obviously review this proposal to determine the proper response," Loctite Chairman David Freeman said in a statement from the company's headquarters in Hartford, Conn.
Henkel said its managing director, Hans-Dietrich Winkhaus, had met Freeman over the weekend and informed him of the company's acquisition proposal.
"Henkel offered to start talks with Loctite aimed at a swift and friendly takeover," the company said in a statement.
Henkel said it had told Loctite that it might decide to make a public takeover bid if the talks failed to make progress or foundered.
Henkel also said that it viewed its current stake in Loctite as a permanent investment and did not plan to sell it.
In a related development, the rating agency Standard & Poor's said it placed Henkel's debt on CreditWatch with negative implications. About $160 million of Henkel's rated debt is affected, it said.
S&P said the proposed acquisition would double Henkel's debt.

"From a business perspective, the acquisition of Loctite, which is one of its largest competitors, would strongly reinforce Henkel's global No. 1 position in both industrial and consumer adhesives," it said.
"The acquisition of a U.S. company would also improve its geographical sales split, which currently is biased toward Europe (80 percent of sales)," S&P said in a statement.
